Subject: Private endpoint egress requirements - need IPs & firewall confirmation

Hi Alex,

We're preparing our network change window for the Redwood private deployment and our compliance team needs a formal list of outbound IPs and the recommended firewall rules to allow the control plane + model-serving heads to reach Redwood's endpoints. Specifically we need: 1) definitive egress IP allowlist (CIDRs and single IPs), 2) ports and protocols, 3) TLS requirements (SNI/mTLS), 4) DNS expectations (do you require split-horizon?), and 5) logging/audit expectations for SOC scope.

Can you provide a certifiable artifact we can attach to the change ticket (NETOPS-4721)? We'll be gating the change on the network team's approval.

Thanks,
Marissa Ng
NetOps, Orchid Health

From: alex_martinez@redwood.ai

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress requirements - need IPs & firewall confirmation

Marissa — thanks for the clear checklist. I've attached a concise IP list and an example proxy/NAT configuration for your ops team. High level answers up front: 

- Egress IPs: we publish a small stable set of outbound IPs for control-plane calls and model fetch. See attachment: redwood-egress-ip-list.csv. We recommend allowing the listed /32s and a CIDR for transient burst pools (only required if you opt into burst routing).
- Ports: 443 (HTTPS) required for all control+data traffic. 853 only if you use our DOH health checks (optional).
- TLS: mandatory TLS 1.2+ with SNI. For private deployments we strongly recommend mTLS for the control plane—certificate exchange is handled via our KMS integration during onboarding. We can provide certs or accept your CA-signed certs.
- DNS: we support both split-horizon and public DNS. If you route via a private resolver, ensure forwarders allow queries to redwood's service domain; don't NAT DNS responses to different A records.
- Auditing: we emit connection logs and request traces to the private control plane logs. For SOC evidence we can provide an export window covering the change date.

Action items for us:
1) Attach the CSV with the final IPs (redwood-egress-ip-list.csv).
2) Confirm whether Orchid will enforce mTLS for control-plane (reply yes/no).
3) If Orchid wants burst routing, confirm you need the burst CIDR expanded.

Attachments: redwood-egress-ip-list.csv (CSV), egress-proxy-config.example.txt (text)

Regards,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Looping in a couple of compliance and sales touchpoints with a few clarifications for Orchid's auditors: 

Marissa — quick clarifications from a compliance viewpoint: 
- We can produce a signed PDF attesting to the IP set and the date/time range it applies to; we'll include a hash and version number.
- For mTLS: if Orchid requires mutual TLS for control plane, our onboarding will require a certificate exchange. For the SOC artifact, we can provide the certificate thumbprints used during the onboarding window.
- Data plane: customer payloads are sent over TLS and are not persisted in our control plane logs beyond request headers and flow metadata unless you request enhanced trace logging (opt-in).

I've prep'd a short set of firewall rule examples below you can paste into change tickets: 
1) Allow outbound TCP 443 to x.x.x.11, x.x.x.12 (redwood control-plane /32s)
2) Allow outbound TCP 443 to 203.0.113.0/28 (model-serving bloom/burst pool; only if burst routing enabled)
3) Allow DNS (UDP 53 / TCP 53) to your resolver only; ensure resolver can reach our service FQDNs.

If Orchid's procurement needs an SLA exception or written confirmation for a specific IP set freeze window, let us know and we'll route to ops leadership.

- Lauren Bishop
Head of Trust & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — quick confirmation from SecureLabs (third-party assessor): we've reviewed the CSV and the proxy sample. A few recommendations prior to certification:

- Harden the proxy config to drop TLS renegotiation and enforce TLS1.3 on the outward path when possible. Document fallback to TLS1.2 and note where it's used.
- Publish a short-runbook item to verify IP list consistency: verify the /32s every 24hrs vs a signed list stored in your S3 artifact bucket.
- For DNS: avoid split-horizon responses that rewrite redwood's A records; prefer resolver-forwarding to prevent cache poisoning.

Marissa — if you can confirm mTLS is required or optional we'll mark the ticket as "controls satisfied" in our report.

-- Mike Jensen
Principal Network Assessor, SecureLabs
